- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to recent price drops; fails to adjust downward when true prices show strong downward momentum.
- Overestimation is more pronounced when historical prices are volatile or show recent spikes.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp spikes, underestimating continuation of trend.
- Forecasts often overshoot after a spike, then correct too quickly, missing the true long-term direction.
- Model underestimates downward trends in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) but become more accurate later (5–10 days) — suggesting a lag in short-term sensitivity.
- Model fails to capture the true “tail risk” or extreme price movements, especially in the final 3–5 days of the forecast.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the historical price trend is stable or trending upward, but underperform during sharp reversals or volatility spikes.
